title: PASS 4: an execution can be enqueued with NO plan — the 'every run starts from a RECORDED plan' invariant (D-486) is not enforced at the enqueue chokepoint
class: an invariant enforced at some entry points and asserted for all of them (self-reporting control)
surface: POST /api/s4-execution-jobs (views.py:4535 → execution_engine/intake.py:enqueue_s4_execution, plan_id Optional=None); the same intake serves POST /claims/<id>/run and /claims/<id>/run-async
reproduction: on scratch, as an admin (tenant 1): plant an approved claim with an active metadata recipe; POST /api/s4-execution-jobs {test_id, environment_id: 4} with no plan → 202 {job_id: 131, status: queued}; SELECT plan_id FROM s4_execution_jobs WHERE id=131 → NULL. Two earlier attempts were refused for OTHER reasons (environment scope; no executable recipe) — none of the refusals was 'no plan'
evidence: job 131 queued on scratch with plan_id NULL, created_by 15; intake.enqueue_s4_execution signature `plan_id: Optional[str] = None`; the route's own docstring names a production-confirm gate and an admin gate and no plan gate; D-486 records 'every execution starts from a RECORDED plan … /run retired', and the memory ledger already counts 568 plan-less stamped runs since the re-enable as evidence
expected: a loud refusal naming the missing plan, at the ONE execution chokepoint, for every entry point
observed: the release, requirement and schedule entry points plan first; the API and the two claim-level routes hand the intake a job with no plan and it accepts it — the invariant holds by convention of the caller, not by the chokepoint
proposed_fix: make plan_id REQUIRED in enqueue_s4_execution and refuse without it (PlanRefused), then either point the claim-level routes and the API at the planner (plan-for-one-claim) or retire them as /run was; add a guard test that enqueues without a plan through every route and asserts the refusal. The 568 plan-less runs already on production are the evidence this path is exercised
closure: D-494 (merge 1eb64a8, 2026-09-15): the plan requirement enforced at intake/sync/worker; every S4 path refuses first naming the plan

title: PASS 4 #2: Evaluate WRITES a recorded GO decision over zero checks for a release whose only declared target is an inactive environment — while the release board says it will refuse
class: a list must not contradict the page it links to (D-491), and a gate must not read GO over nothing
surface: /releases (board card) vs /releases/<id>?tab=decision (quality decision card) — hostile release AUD-release-inactive-env: one requirement (79 approved claims), one target: an environment with is_active=false
reproduction: plant a release with one requirement of 79 approved claims and declare a single target environment that is inactive (scripts/audit/hostile_world.py); GET /releases → the card reads 'Evaluate will refuse — 79 items in scope are not current · 1 requirement · 0 of 79 functional checks current'; GET /releases/<id>?tab=decision → data-recommendation="go", 'targets (declared): AUD-inactive: 0 of 0 checks current', 'no rule triggered', 'Grading Nothing ungraded'
evidence: counts.py + the page fragments: the board counts the 79 claims as in-scope-and-not-current; the decision preview scopes to the declared (inactive) target, finds 0 checks, and with nothing to grade recommends GO; the recorded decision row (planted) reads CANNOT DETERMINE beside it; PASS 4 attack #2 on scratch, as admin: POST /releases/<id>/evaluate-decision → a new release_decisions row, recommendation=go, on the inactive-only release (decisions 13 → 14); the preview had already read GO over '0 of 0 checks current'; PASS 4 attack #9 on the NO-SCOPE release (zero requirements, zero claims): Evaluate was not refused — it recorded decision 32, recommendation=go, criteria_met every axis true, policy Plimsol default v1, plan NULL. The inactive-only release recorded decision 33 the same way. Both are the same defect: the policy grades an EMPTY input as satisfied on all six axes
expected: one answer: an inactive-only target is either refused (no active environment in scope — the D-485 interim) on BOTH surfaces, or evaluated on both; and a preview with zero checks never reads GO
observed: the list says refuse, the page previews GO, and Evaluate RECORDS GO — a release can be recommended and recorded GO by deactivating its only target environment after declaring it; nothing was checked
proposed_fix: Evaluate must REFUSE (cannot_determine, no row) when the resolved scope holds zero checks or zero active environments — D9's 'ungraded inputs block GO' applied to an empty input, and D-484's 'Evaluate refuses non-current scope' applied to no scope at all; the board and the tab call the same scope filter (D-491); page tests over a no-scope release and an inactive-only target
closure: D-496 (merge bbd943f, 2026-09-18): a decision requires a non-empty graded scope — the engine refuses before the policy runs; the board and the page from the same call; production's two GO rows audited, none empty

title: PASS 4 #1: a PASS verdict for a run that does not exist is insertable — s6_interpretations.run_id has no foreign key to s4_execution_runs
class: an invariant the ledger states that the schema does not hold (the readers happen to join through runs)
surface: tenant schema: s6_interpretations (verdicts) → s4_execution_runs (runs); pg_constraint lists NO foreign key on run_id
reproduction: INSERT INTO s6_interpretations (run_id, recipe_id, claim_test_id, outcome, verdict, detail) VALUES (<random uuid>, <random uuid>, <a claim>, 'passed', 'passed', '{}') → accepted; SELECT count(*) FROM s6_interpretations i WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM s4_execution_runs r WHERE r.run_id = i.run_id) → 1
evidence: D-466 records that PASS requires positive attestation over captured evidence; that holds in the interpreter's writer, not in the table. The decision path reads verdicts through a join on s4_execution_runs (_COUNTED_RUNS_BULK_SQL), so the orphan is invisible to grading today — the invariant is held by every reader's join, not by the schema
expected: a verdict cannot exist without the run it interprets: a foreign key, and a guard that no verdict row is orphaned
observed: a PASS with no run behind it sits in the table; any reader that lists verdicts without the join would count it
proposed_fix: add the FK (ON DELETE CASCADE with the run's own retention), verify zero orphans on production before applying, and add a schema test that every verdict's run exists
closure: fk_s6_interpretations_run (s6_interpretations.run_id -> s4_execution_runs.run_id, NO ACTION) in migration 20260919_0010 after a read-only zero-orphan proof on production (3,691 rows, 0 orphans); proven by attempting an orphan insert and a run delete; the run_id census gate (tests/integration/test_constraints_triage.py) fails on any new unledgered run_id column

title: a DEACTIVATED user keeps acting for the life of the access token (30 minutes): users.is_active is never read on a request, and the API deactivate route commits the flag directly, bypassing the service that revokes refresh tokens

reproduction: scratch: as admin POST /api/users/14/deactivate -> 204, users.is_active=false; then with user 14's still-valid cookie: GET /requirements 200, GET /api/releases 200, POST /requirements/<id>/edit 302 and the row CHANGED ('deactivated user still edits'); the user's two live refresh_tokens rows stayed unrevoked after the API deactivate; POST /api/auth/refresh as the deactivated user -> 401 (refresh does check the flag), so the window is the access token's 30 minutes
evidence: claims_probe.json; the refresh-token proof; CLAUDE.md's own text: 'Role downgrade → revokes all refresh tokens so stale access-tokens expire quickly'
expected: deactivation ends the session: the flag is read at the auth chokepoint (one indexed read per request, or a short-lived cache), and every deactivate path revokes refresh tokens
observed: an offboarded user acts for up to 30 minutes, and via the API route their refresh tokens are left live (harmless only because refresh re-checks the flag)
proposed_fix: read users.is_active in require_auth/login_required (fail closed); route the API deactivate through the service; a guard test that a deactivated session is refused on the next request
closure: users.is_active read at the one auth chokepoint every request passes (fail closed); the API deactivate/activate routes go through the service; the last-superadmin guard in the service; the revocation failure logged; the AST guard test_deactivation_paths.py
